rows.question: is the target of a collection authorized by the server, not by the caller's role?

probes.expected: refused (409/422) with no approved scope
probes.observed: 409 {"detail":{"error":"scope_not_configured","reason":"no approved network scope — CryptoScan refuses to probe until a scope names the exact destinations"}}

probes.expected: 422 when the approved scope names a /8
422 when the scope names 169.254.169.254
422 when the scope names 127.0.0.1
2xx for one exact host:port
refused for a host outside the approved scope
refused for a CIDR in the request itself
4xx for a target outside CRYPTOSCAN_SOURCE_ROOTS
probes.observed: 400 {"detail":"repo_url: source path /etc is outside the allowed source roots"}

unproven: which hosts a bank has *approved* is deployment data; this row proves the refusal paths, not that a given CIDR list is the right one
limits: the per-collector matrix for these questions is guide 116
the traffic budget and window are measured by guide 116's probes

Executed in-process against the real app and a temporary SQLite database. Authorization decisions are the server's own; what is not proven is the deployment around it (reverse proxy, identity provider, network policy).

A permitted request is not a completed one: this drill asks whether the guard let the caller through, not whether the handler then did something useful. A 5xx past the guard still counts as past the boundary.
Empty request bodies mean body-level validation is not exercised; tenant isolation is a separate drill (guide 124).
